..
Issued at 1047 PM CST Sun Nov 15 2026

Mid evening surface observations depicted widespread gentle
saturated upslope boundary layer flow, with light southeast
winds. As expected, the stratus persisted all of Sunday, with 
a daily temperature range of 2 degrees (38 to 40) all day at
DDC. Nighttime microphysics satellite imagery depicted
widespread stratus across much of the plains, including the
western half of Kansas. Stratus will hold tonight, and through
at least the first half of Monday, with temperatures again
moving very little in the 30s - but well above freezing. Areas
of fog are probable through Monday morning, particularly western
zones, as the stratus layer nocturnally lowers to near the
ground. Elevated south winds should keep any visibility
restrictions limited. 

South winds will increase noticeably Monday, as return flow
establishes on the back side of retreating high pressure. 
NBM wind grids were about 2-3 kts too low, and increased them,
with gusts of 30-35 mph by afternoon. Although a south wind,
this will be recirculated continental polar air, and it will 
not be pleasant. NBM was also a few degrees too warm Monday 
afternoon, and lowered 2-3 degrees. Stratus will be very 
stubborn to erode Monday afternoon, and with 850 mb temperatures
only rebounding to the +4-5C range, afternoon temperatures will
struggle through the 40s, with some places achieving 50 degrees
briefly around 3 pm. 

Stronger south winds are expected Tuesday, as a potent 
shortwave advances east through the Great Basin, and southerly 
850 mb winds increase to 45-50 mph. 18z MAV MOS depicts 
sustained south winds near 30 mph at DDC at noon Tuesday, with 
gusts easily in the 40-45 mph range. With the additional forced 
mechanical mixing, the residual cool air will mix out, allowing 
temperatures to rebound to within a few degrees of 60. 

Great Basin shortwave will weaken significantly and eject well
to the north of SW KS Wednesday. Wednesday will feature
noticeably warmer afternoon temperatures, as elevated to strong
SWly downslope winds overspread SW KS. NBM guidance in the 
upper 60s appears reasonable, about 10 degrees above normal. 
Morning lows will be much milder by Wednesday as well, well into
the 40s. 

Unseasonably mild pleasant weather will continue Thursday, as
midlevel heights temporarily rise between passing shortwaves.
NBM guidance of afternoon temperatures in the 60s matches MEX
guidance. Elevated southeast winds will begin the moisture
advection process, but with no forcing evident, Thursday's
forecast remains dry. 

Models place a large powerful trough along the west coast
6 pm Thursday, and the global models show good agreement with
a strong lead shortwave ejecting out of this trough onto the
plains late Friday. Associated lee cyclogenesis is progged to
be near NW KS 6 pm Friday, with NBM pops for showers and
thunderstorms in the chance category ahead of the associated
cold front and lee trough/dryline. Thunderstorm development
appears probable late Friday; we will need to monitor for 
severe potential/storm mode through the week. As is the case in
November, the question will be one of instability and moisture 
availability. Kinematics will be excellent to support organized 
convection, with 500 mb flow near 60 kts, and bulk shear near 
50 kts. Models struggle to bring north anything more than 
highly modified gulf moisture, with dewpoints in the mid 50s the
likely outcome. Organized convective line structures are 
likely. NBM pops in the chance category favoring the eastern 
zones are appropriate for now. This system is now modeled to be
far more progressive than previous model runs. As such, dry 
weather is expected to return across Kansas next weekend. Still
- no killing freezes in the 20s in sight through the upcoming 
week.
